title: Patient Payment Plan Training Bulletin: Time an Open Assistance Case Still Needs
content:
While the open financial assistance case is still being completed or decided, the pause period for installments on a **Patient Payment Plan** is longer by the time the case still needs. A financial assistance application of the patient is open when one of the patient's financial assistance cases in the Financial Assistance Program (Charity Care) stands in submitted or pending documents status, a submitted case being taken first. The case's status, documents due date and determination days are read from the case in the Financial Assistance Program (Charity Care).

**Rule.** When the case stands in pending documents status the pause period gains the days from the handling date to the case's documents due date (none once that date has passed) plus the case's determination days, the time for the requested documents to arrive and the case to be decided; when it stands in submitted status it gains the case's determination days alone; and it gains nothing when no application is open.

**Q. The case is waiting on documents due ten days from today. What does the pause period gain?**
A. The 10 days to the documents due date plus the case's determination days.

**Q. The documents due date passed last week and the case still stands in pending documents status.**
A. No days to the documents due date (that date has passed); the pause period gains the case's determination days.

**Q. The case stands in submitted status.**
A. The case's determination days alone.

**Q. No case stands in submitted or pending documents status.**
A. Nothing.

Hypothetical: with determination days of 25, a pending-documents case due in 10 days adds 35 days; a submitted case adds 25.
